subject: Ridgetop: request for cryptographic response signatures - prioritization
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ridgetop: request for cryptographic response signatures - prioritization

Hi team,

Quick one from the Ridgetop execs — they confirmed last night that a signed, auditable response for every model output is a gating requirement for production. Summary of the ask (attached spec): they want a cryptographic signature tied to each completed response that includes the request id, model id, and a timestamp, and an easy verification path for their systems/legal. They also want rotation/retirement semantics in the audit logs.

Context: this is a $1.1M ARR two-year committed deal and they are asking for a pilot within 3 weeks so they can close next month. Deal id RIDG-2026-042.

Ask: can product/eng scope this, give a recommended MVP (minimally viable approach we can ship fast), and a ballpark estimate to include in our proposal? If we can offer a pilot that signs final (non-streaming) responses within 3–4 weeks, we can move forward; the customer is willing to accept a phased approach.

Attachments: Ridgetop_Signing_Spec.pdf (customer doc)

Thanks — I know it’s non-trivial but this is a close-critical ask.
Grace
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ridgetop: request for cryptographic response signatures - prioritization

Thanks Grace — reading the spec now. A few clarifying Qs for the team and for the customer:

1) Acceptance criteria: does Ridgetop need signatures for every token (streaming) or only for completed responses (end-of-response)? The spec indicates they primarily need end-of-response verification for audit trails.
2) Threat model: do they require HSM-backed keys / third-party CA attestation, or is a Redwood-managed key with rotation sufficient for the first pilot?
3) Verification flow: do they need an online verification endpoint from us, or do we provide a public key + signature and they verify on their side?

Initial thinking: we could implement this as a serving-runtime middleware that signs the final output and attaches an "X-Response-Signature" header plus a signed payload blob in the response envelope. That keeps streaming and HSM questions out of scope for an MVP.

Marcus — can you weigh in on feasibility/latency and recommend an MVP scope? If we aim for non-streamed responses + verification docs + audit export entries, I think product could push this as a contract commitment (pilot) with a phased implementation for streaming/HSM.

Karthik
Product Manager

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ridgetop: request for cryptographic response signatures - prioritization

Thanks — technical notes / estimate below (high level):

- Options:
  * MVP-A: Best-effort signing with an internal signing service (ECDSA) using a Redwood-managed key. Fast to implement (~3–4 engineer-weeks), attaches signature at response finalization only, not for streaming. Verification done client-side with public key we publish.
  * MVP-B: HSM-backed signing + rotation + attestation. Higher compliance profile but requires HSM integrations and key rotation automation (~10–12 engineer-weeks), possible infra cost and security review.

- Latency: ECDSA signing adds ~1–3ms per response in the sign-and-package path for non-streamed responses. The bigger risk is synchronous signing under load — we'll need to batch or async sign in the request finalizer to avoid tail-latency spikes.

- Streaming: supporting streaming signatures is substantially more complex (requires incremental signatures or chunk-level HMACs and changes to our streaming wire protocol). We should explicitly scope streaming out of the pilot.

- Audit/export: we can add a compact signature metadata row to the existing audit exports (request id, signature, key id, timestamp) — low effort to add.

- Suggested MVP scope for pilot:
  1) Sign only completed, non-streamed responses using ECDSA with a Redwood-managed key.
  2) Provide public verification endpoint + verification docs.
  3) Add signature metadata to audit export and per-request tracing.
  4) Deliver a short security FAQ and key-rotation plan.

Estimate (end-to-end for MVP above): 4–6 engineer-weeks (small cross-functional sprint) + security review. I'll attach a quick impact spreadsheet.

If product wants to push this as a short-term commitment to Ridgetop, we need to lock scope to the above. Anything beyond (HSM, streaming) becomes a roadmap project.

Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachment: engineering-impact-estimate.xlsx

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ridgetop: request for cryptographic response signatures - prioritization

Thanks for the thread — a couple of negotiation/CS notes from my side:

- Ridgetop is happy to accept a phased delivery if we can commit to a clear pilot cadence. They want evidence (test vectors + verification tool) before they flip the switch.
- From a commercial perspective, we should include language in the MSA addendum describing the pilot scope and the future roadmap items (HSM, streaming) as separate billable phases.
- CS can own the pilot coordination and verification testing once we have an internal build and docs. 

If product/eng can commit to delivering the MVP (non-streamed ECDSA signing + audit export + docs) for a pilot targeted at 2026-10-21, I will lock the pilot dates with the customer and update the mutual action plan.

Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the concrete MVP suggestion — that scope works for Ridgetop for a pilot.

Next steps I propose:
1) Product & Eng: confirm resource owners and sign up for the 4–6 week delivery target (pilot build by 2026-10-21). Marcus, can you confirm the core eng leads and any blockers by EOD Mon?
2) Security/Product: Naomi/Karthik, prepare a one-page security/attestation note for legal by 2026-10-07.
3) CS/Sales: Marissa/Grace will lock pilot dates and send an updated mutual action plan to Ridgetop Legal (attached) once we have confirmation.

We will take the streaming/HSM work to the product roadmap backlog as a follow-up. Thanks all — we will flag any scope creep early.

Grace
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
